text.p: The following is a direct contribution from commodity statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

In spite of the widespread feeling that London is overbought after this week's rally, there were few sellers amid frost fears in Brazil in the coming weeks. Benchmark July was up $4 at $2,086 per tonne, while September lost $2 to close at $2,098 per tonne. Prices can be expected to remain firm until the end of the Brazilian frost season.

Arabica futures in New York ended mostly lower in thin pre-holiday trade as speculators took profits following two straight sessions of hefty gains. July lost 3.45 cents/lb to close at 256.85 cents/lb. September closed 3.90 cents/lb lower at 226.05 cents/lb. Despite today's downturn, industry sources said a continued supply crunch was likely to keep the market well underpinned in the coming months. Traders continued to monitor weather forecasts for top-grower Brazil. A cold front moved into Brazil's coffee belt, but no damaging cold is expected.

UNITED STATES - Coffee roastings during the week ended May 17 totalled about 300,000 60-kg bags, down from 330,000 bags the previous week and 310,000 bags in the corresponding week a year ago, Complete Coffee Coverage said. Cumulative roastings totalled 6.625 million bags versus 6.500 million bags in the same year-ago period.

DOMINICAN REPUBLIC - According to official sources coffee production in mid-May reached 513,633 60-kg bags. Total production in 1995/96 (July/June) reached 798,255 60-kg bags, up from 706,780 bags produced in 1994/95.

ANGOLA - Angola is seeking to lift coffee production back to levels seen in the colonial era as part of its efforts to revive the war-ravaged economy, official sources said. Before Angola gained independence from Portugal in 1975 it was Africa's second largest producer of coffee, harvesting around 3.8 million bags. Robusta production in 1996/97 (April/March) was a meagre 82,000 bags, up from 53,000 bags produced the previous year and 25,000 bags produced in 1994/95.

RWANDA - According to official sources coffee production in Rwanda in 1996/97 (April/March) reached 265,000 60-kg bags, down from 354,000 bags produced the previous year. However, exports as reported by the International Coffee Organization in London even point to a lower crop in 1996/97.

TANZANIA - Tanzania exported 583,400 bags of coffee in July/March 1996/97, 8 per cent less than was exported the same period in 1995/96. Total exports in crop year 1995/96 reached 921,000 bags, up from 612,000 bags exported the previous year. Main countries of destination in July/March 1996/97 were Germany (231,200 vs 235,100 bags) and Japan (93,900 vs 108,600 bags).
